newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cerus says Valeo sale to raise 6.5 bln Fr.
newsitem.headline: Cerus says Valeo sale to raise 6.5 bln Fr.

text.p: Cerus, a holding company owned by Italy's Carlo de Benedetti, said on Tuesday the sale of its stake in Valeo car parts maker to CGIP and others would raise 6.5 billion francs and a possible 0.2 billion francs more.

The group said in a statement it was selling at 330 francs per share, with 20.26 percent of Valeo going to French holding CGIP, 3.63 percent to JP Morgan and GT Corporation and another 3.55 percent to French state-owned bank CDC.

It said it would use to proceeds for debt repayment and its own needs. Valeo is making an advance dividend downpayment of 10 francs a share which Cerus will have rights to and there is also a conditional further payment of 10 francs a share in dividends if Valeo's 1997 net profits equal at least 1.45 billion francs.

CGIP said in a separate statement that it had a share swap agreement with JP Morgan, which has taken 3.6 percent while the investment bank said it planned to sell its new holding on in three to five years.
Cerus said it would make a capital gain of 4.17 billion francs.
Among the debt repayments planned, Cerus cited credit lines from banks worth 1.3 billion francs due in March 1997 and bonds to the tune of 0.3 billion francs.
On another 4.75 percent July 1996 convertible loan, the firm said it would carry out an early amortisation.
"Cerus will continue to divest financial and property assets and seek controlling stakes in the industrial and service domains," the Cerus statement added.
